terms.definition: A tightly coiled strand of DNA and protein that carries an organism's genetic instructions.
One of two identical copies that make up a duplicated chromosome, joined to its twin at the centromere.
The pinched, narrow region where two sister chromatids are held together.
DNA wound repeatedly around histone proteins and folded further so that nearly two meters of DNA per cell fits inside a microscopic nucleus; this coiling is what gives a chromosome its compact shape.
The pattern of individual genes sitting at fixed positions strung along a chromosome's DNA, similar to houses spaced along a street, each carrying instructions for a particular trait or protein.
A specific segment of DNA on a chromosome that contains instructions for one trait or function.
The loosely spread-out form of DNA and protein found in the nucleus when a cell is not dividing.
A protein that DNA wraps around, helping it coil up tightly to fit inside the nucleus.
The compartment inside a cell where chromosomes are stored.
A protein fiber that attaches to a chromosome's centromere and pulls sister chromatids apart during cell division.
One version of a gene; different alleles at the same spot on a chromosome can produce different versions of a trait.
